title: [Need Advice] Add @required annotation using PROPERTY_USAGE_REQUIRED

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Edit: Renamed from @export_required to @required

This prototype adds an annotation `@required` that can be used as a second annotation for exported properties. It will issue a configuration warning if the property's value equals Variant::NIL. It does this by automatically adding the new enum value `PROPERTY_USAGE_REQUIRED` to the property usages, which is later checked in the Node's `update_configuration_warnings` function against every property to populate automatic warnings.

Draft status reason:
~~This PR adds a conditional to the GDScriptInstance::set hotpath. This is required to issue `update_configuration_warnings` when a required property's value changes. Sure, it is covered by a #ifdef TOOLS_ENABLED and Engine.is_editor_hint so it'll have no impact in build, but I don't love how the fairly neat and clean function has this block added into it, which is irrelevant to the rest of the function code.~~ Removed. Now configuration warnings are for @required are only updated on scene save. I mainly need advice on four things:
1. Is there some place else where I can setup this kind of functionality instead? I was looking at the `editor_inspector`, since it already has a bunch of code related to property value changes. Of course, this would limit the configuration warning changes to only the changes made by the inspector.
2. ~~The `PropertyUsageHint` enum feels a bit sacred. Is it fine to add another value to it?~~ Looks like modern systems should support up-to 64 properties in this enum and we have 29.
3. Annotations are clearly a feature that should only be added-to or changed after a lot of deliberation. Is there even a chance of this PR getting merged?
4. Does anyone see the point of comparing it to falsey values of other types? Right now, this is only effective for property types inheriting `Object` as it attempts to check the property value against Variant::NIL.  Assuming what's "empty" on non-reference types feels like one step too far into the land of PHP/Js horrors.
